candidate_law.name: replacement quantity-quality capability law
candidate_law.setup: A formation begins with personnel P0 and experience E. It loses fraction ell, leaving p=1-ell of original personnel with survivor experience E. It then receives r*P0 replacements of experience E_R. All non-personnel/non-experience capability factors and effective-readiness fractions are held fixed.
candidate_law.one_for_one_corollary: If r=ell, headcount is fully restored but C_after/C_before=1-ell*(1-q).
candidate_law.full_restoration_condition: The replacement amount r_star that restores pre-loss capability is the unique nonnegative solution of (p+r_star)^(-0.28)*(p+r_star*q)=1.

analytic_predictions: If E_R<E and ell>0, one-for-one headcount replacement leaves a strictly positive capability deficit ell*(1-q).
Because E and E_R are clamped to [0,1], q is at least 0.6. Therefore the capability ratio is strictly increasing in replacement amount r for all valid Pineland experience values.
The full-capability replacement requirement is unique and exceeds the one-for-one replacement amount whenever E_R<E.
At equal loss fraction, lower replacement experience requires more replacement personnel to restore the same capability.
production_equivalence_required: For valid E_R<=E cases with positive remaining personnel, direct production capability() ratios must match the closed-form law at floating-point tolerance when all other factors are fixed.
One-for-one replacement cases must match the exact 1-ell*(1-q) corollary.
Numerical root solutions for r_star must reproduce capability ratio 1 within 1e-12 and must exceed ell whenever E_R<E.
claim_boundary: SL9 is a conditional theorem of Pineland's synthetic replacement-memory and combat-capability equations. It does not state a real military replacement ratio.
